key_catalyst: Chip rebound led by Micron +5% and AMD +5% (Microsoft to deploy AMD Helios racks on Azure) lifting the Nasdaq 100 despite the morning's Iran/oil and AI-selloff SELL thesis.
reasoning: The morning SELL thesis rested on an escalating Iran/Hormuz oil shock layered on an AI-trade SECTOR_ROTATION selloff, but neither catalyst produced fresh intraday follow-through in the 9:30-15:45 window: no new Hormuz-blockade or oil-surge headline hit, and instead the live intraday catalysts were chip-POSITIVE (Micron +5%, AMD +5% on the Microsoft/Azure Helios deal, Alphabet gaining on its new Gemini chip). QQQ drifted only -0.87% — a muted decline, not the capitulation or accelerating panic a live escalating shock would produce. What remains unresolved is the latent Middle East/oil tail that could re-price in the Asia/Europe overnight session, but nothing in this window objectively escalated into the close.
